newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen weighed down by supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen weighed down by supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil levels were seen softer on Wednesday with incoming supplies placing pressures on prices, traders said.
"The arbitrage from the US Gulf is open and I think there is at least one cargo already heading east," said a trader.
Traders said besides the usual term supplies, Kuwait was projected to have exported three spot cargoes of around 80,000 tonnes each in January. One cargo was reported sold to a major.
"The second cargo has also been committed and is on its way here," said a trader.
"The third cargo has yet to be sold and will be loading at the end of this month," the trader added.
The usual term supplies that would be heading towards Singapore include six Iranian and one Venzuelan cargoes, traders said. Most of which is expected to be placed in the bunker market, they said.
On demand, traders in China said activities are coming to a halt with the start of preparations for the Chinese New year holidays.
January swaps edged down slightly and was last quoted at $120.50/$122.00 per tonne, from Tuesday's $121.25-$122.25.
